visuallyConfirmedRules: The group declares kill or subdual intent before combat; absent a declaration, attacks use the killing form, and the chosen form cannot change for that dragon.
The text names dragon categories that cannot be subdued and bars creatures with less than average intelligence from attacking to subdue.
Once subdual intent is announced, attack damage against the dragon is nonfatal battering/bruising damage.

At each melee-round end, accumulated subdual damage is compared with the dragon's hit points to set a percentile chance; a percentile result equal to or below the chance subdues it, and a 1:1-or-higher ratio is automatic.
At most one human-sized attacker per three linear feet of exposed dragon body, excluding the tail; a fully exposed 15-foot body allows 11 attackers.
The worked example carries damage across rounds: 44/88 = 50%, 67/88 is treated as 76%, 77/88 is treated as 88%; a roll of 89 fails, then 12 further damage crosses 1:1 and subdues automatically.

The adjacent Length of Subdual passage covers indefinite duration, holding/treatment/treasure/freedom conditions, older and intelligent dragons' behavior, alignment-dependent escape/kill likelihood, and no second subdual until freedom is regained.
separateAdjacentContent: The Value of a Subdued Dragon sale-price passage is separately inventoried as mm-subdued-dragon in the economic closure; it is not a second money finding here.
The Dragon's Breath effectiveness chart is a separate table, not a subdual step. This review inspected its presence but did not adjudicate its separate owner/scope join.

source.layout: Common Golem introduction followed by separate Clay, Flesh, Iron, and Stone profiles/construction passages; Stone continuation on p.49.
boundedConstructionProcedureParts: creator-level prerequisites and type-specific required spell combinations
type-specific body/material preparation and construction/ritual steps
type-specific creation failure, control, and operational outcomes
visuallyConfirmedExamples: Clay: lawful-good cleric level 17 or higher (a magical tome allows a lower-level cleric); resurrection, animate objects, commune, prayer, and bless; fashion a man-shaped clay statue and complete an uninterrupted ritual; 20,000 gp spell materials plus at least 30,000 gp vestments; a cumulative 1% per melee round risk of chaotic-evil spirit possession and permanent loss of control if it occurs.

Flesh: magical tome or magic-user level 14 or higher with wish, polymorph any object, geas, protection from normal missiles, and strength; 1,000 gp per hit point in materials; one month; creator commands/suspends it; separate cumulative berserk and possible control-recovery chances.

Iron: magical tome or magic-user level 18 or higher with wish, polymorph any object, geas, and cloud kill; 1,000 gp per hit point in materials; three months; creator control and simple-command/guard behavior.

Stone: magic-user level 16 or higher with wish, polymorph any object, geas, and slow; 1,000 gp per hit point in materials; two months; creator control and simple commands. The p.49 continuation gives additional stone-golem operating/defense details.
source.sharedAdjacentRule: The p.47 common prose states that magical creatures with hit dice equal to or greater than the golem can attack effectively; use 4.5 hit points per hit die, rounded up, to determine hit dice, and names hit-die totals by golem type. This is a shared rules statement, distinct from the excluded full profile stat cells.
